text: The raw dumps were under a root-only traversable directory; tightened modes and umask for the temporary tarball and all new dumps as well. No evidence of reads.

Removed deploy root rsync (CI uses tar), stopped root PHP execution in orders, disabled unlisted contractor jpark, restricted unauthenticated cache support actions, denied scripts in uploads. No successful SSH for jpark in restored logs.
CI release uses push with no agent. Removed unused inbound CI self-key and unlisted jpark login. Constrained database backup key; restricted repo config and moved Git maintenance out of root context.

WordPress also had an unlisted jpark admin; revoked role/sessions and randomized stale credential. Export tool now gates marketing lists versus support lookups and delivers private CSV as caller rather than root.

Historical invoice corrections match source order totals. Required that match at update time (left existing invoices untouched). Restricted site DB login to web-01, removed unused billing-account writes while retaining payment-key rotation, and disabled LOCAL INFILE.

Disabled PHP write access to application code and browser code editing. CI key limited to the release from CI; password logins for legacy scripts unchanged. Removed root recursive chown over deploy-controlled paths.

Restricted node metrics to office and loopback; Grafana remains accessible with login. Restored auth/syslog to root:adm 0640. Recurring file access events alone do not identify a remote actor; correlating with SSH and service logs.

Backup forced-command tested with a real encrypted archive. CI maintenance now executes only local scripts as deploy, not root or over HTTP, and does not prune active release files. Pinned SSH host verification on release.

The active ride form uses postdata-1. Hardened its local handler to validate uploaded image data before moving it; retained supported photo types, form and moderation. Existing ride JPEG passes the new content check.

Validated the archive hash at both ends; payout batch inputs currently match their source order totals. Removed gateway, bucket and cache secrets from client process arguments. The full offsite cloud route remains a separate pre-existing issue.

Found an unused legacy WordPress payment option; verified by equality check it was NOT the current billing key. Removed the old secret field. 17:15 scheduled settlement succeeded; marketing and support exports succeeded after hardening.
Directly verified post-hardening dump/encryption/rsync, including pinned SSH host key; previous scheduled archive contained both databases and matched the ci-01 digest.

Office address is shared by multiple staff; Wei used the same SSH fingerprint and checked uploads/CSS on mobile. No anomalous privilege use found. Did not block shared networks or force mass staff password resets.
17:15 batch sent all ten payouts. A subsequent legitimate bookkeeping adjustment matched order LC-20205; monitoring found no unauthorized DB account or billing change.
Scheduled releases remained successful through 17:18. Latest manual DB dump digest matched; no unexpected hooks, maintenance steps, or unauthorized logins found.

Release artifact checksums on web-01 match the 17:18 CI build. Verified public pages, photo, sitemap, dashboard health, DB reports and payouts. External offsite uploads still fail DNS/no route, predating the shift.
